items.title: Incomplete External Statistics
items.text:
Incomplete External Statistics
I have an interesting problem with the external statics reported by proxmox.

I have an influx database on a VM E running on proxmox host D.  D is configured to deliver it's stats to E over E's externally available IP address, and that works fine.

I configured another proxmox host Q to also deliver it's statistics to E (to a different database), and I'm only getting some of the values I get for D.

&#x200B;

For D I get the following:

ballooninfo, blockstat, nic and system series for each VM.

blockstat, cpustat, memory, nics and system series for the host.

system series for each storage.

&#x200B;

For Q I get:

system series for each storage.

system series for only one of the 6 VM's running on the host.

&#x200B;

Obviously some stats are getting there, so the firewall etc are all okay, but I can't figure out why I'm only getting some stats and why one random VM and not the others.  The only notable thing about that VM is that its currently shutdown.

&#x200B;

Any idea?

&#x200B;

Edit: Actually, looking at the database, the series for Q are defined but empty...

It should allow you to select which node to monitor if you route all your stats to the same database.  I haven't been able to test that fully since I'm having issues with my remote node (i.e. the one not hosting the VM that contains the database) talking to the database.
Interesting.  I'm having a porblem getting my second proxmox node to talk to the influx database.  What sort of MTU did you need to use?
Yes, for most things I could have put them all into the same chart, but that doesn't work for the gages unfortunatly.

Your probably not going to be able to run proxmox on that nas, but QNAP's own OS, QTS, does have docker support.  The UI is a little lacking, but if you install something like portainer or are willing to use the command line, it's usable.

Note: You don't say if you have individual addresses or a subnet for your VM's.  Subnets will not work with bridged networking on hetzner, you must use routed mode if you have bought a subnet.  The following assumes individual addresses using bridged networking (which is how your pastebin was set up).

&#x200B;

Try this:

&#x200B;

    auto lo
    iface lo inet loopback
    iface lo inet6 loopback
    
    auto enp2s0
    iface enp2s0 inet manual
            up route add -net 144.xxx.xxx.64 netmask 255.255.255.224 gw 144.xxx.xxx.65 dev enp2s0
    
    auto vmbr0
    iface vmbr0 inet static
            address  144.xxx.xxx.70
            netmask  255.255.255.224
            gateway  144.xxx.xxx.65
            bridge_ports enp2s0
            bridge_stp off
            bridge_fd 0
    
    iface vmbr0 inet6 static
            address  2a01:xxx:xxx:1245::2
            netmask  64
            gateway  fe80::1

This is my network config with your details plugged in.  Remember that, for Bridged IPv4 (as in use here), you must define MAC addresses via the robot website and use that MAC when setting up your VM's or containers.

&#x200B;

Edit: Forgot to mention, for IPv6 you have to create a file /etc/sysctl.d/99-networking.conf containing

    net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1

OK, so you havn't yet ordered additional IPv4 address.  If you intend to access VM's hosted on your proxmox install via IPv4, you will need additional IPv4 address, at least one for each intended VM (unless your going to use NAT, but that brings a whole heap of other issues).  If you are happy (and able) to only use IPv6, you don't need additional addresses since you already have an IPv6 /64 subnet.

&#x200B;

If you need to buy IPv4 address, click the "Order additional IPs / Nets" button that should be just under the area you screenshotted.  You will see 5 choices (with appropriate prices which I've removed):

* **One additional IP with costs**
* **One failover IP**
* **One additional subnet /29**
* **One additional subnet /28**
* **One additional subnet /27**

&#x200B;

The first option will give you a single IPv4 address suitable for using with bridged networking.  You can order up to 6 of those per server, but you have to order one at a time.  [This Hetzner Wiki page](https://wiki.hetzner.de/index.php/Virtualisierung/en) gives instructions for generating the required MAC addresses and just put the value in the appropriate place in the VM or container creation wizard.

The bottom three options gives you a subnet of the specified size.  A /29 gives 6 usuable address, a /28 gives 14 usable addresses and a /27 gives 30 usable addresses.  These will NOT work with bridged networking, so the config above will not work for them.  If you decide to go this route, I can help you out with that.

I have no idea how the Failover IP's work with proxmox, I haven't tried them.

&#x200B;

BTW: if your annonomysing a Hetzner IPv6 block, you should blur the last set of numbers before the double colon (the :: ) since that's the cluster that is specific to your subnet.

In theory yes, but I can't help you with that setup.

Also remember that other services your friends need use of (SSH for example) will need to be routed through the same host.
Yes, that was my point.  Just that everything on the VM's that you want to be accessible on the VM's that don't have external IPv4's needs to be routed through the one that does.

I had an issue where, when doing an apt upgrade, some apps were "kept back" (doing apt upgrade again should show you if this is the case for you).  One was certbot and I don't recall the other, but because they were kept back, so were their dependancies and that broke some things including the Proxmox GUI.

If you have any that are kept back, you can just do "apt install <packages>" to update them.  The GUI might start working again immediatly, but I had to restart my server.
